candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture Team,

I’m writing to join AWA’s Talent Network because your work sits exactly where my experience and my heart meet: helping young people and their families through some of the hardest moments of their lives.

For more than 25 years, I have designed and facilitated learning programs, coached leaders and individuals, and coordinated group programs in person and online, in English and in Spanish. Early in my career in Venezuela, I co-facilitated a community prevention program for adolescents sponsored by Empresas Polar, with workshops on substance use and teen pregnancy prevention for teens living near the company’s facilities. That experience showed me how much prevention depends on reaching families in their own language and reality.

This work is also personal. Addiction to alcohol and drugs has touched my own family, and I have lost a young family member to its consequences. I now have four young grandchildren, and the idea of contributing to prevention efforts that protect children like them means a great deal to me.

I believe I could add value to AWA by supporting staff training and onboarding, developing educational workshops for families, especially Spanish-speaking families, or helping coordinate programs so that teens and parents stay engaged and informed. I’m based in Miami, fully bilingual, and comfortable working remotely or on-site in Miami.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to learn how I could support your team and the families you serve.

Warm regards,
Esther Leon
(713) 504-7640 · leoncesther@gmail.com · linkedin.com/in/esther-leon-ld

Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

candidates.cover_letter:
I am writing to express my interest in the Program Operations position within your adolescent mental health PHP/IOP program. With approximately 12 years of experience working with individuals with autism, behavioral challenges, and social-emotional needs, I bring a strong foundation in behavioral support, staff training, leadership, and program structure. My professional background has allowed me to develop a thorough understanding of what it takes to create safe, consistent, and supportive environments for both clients and staff.

My experience began at Ramapo for Children, where I worked in several capacities, including lifeguard, swim instructor, and Toolbox Specialist. During my time there, I worked closely with neurodiverse individuals and those with behavioral and emotional challenges. As a Toolbox Specialist, I developed and implemented individualized behavioral strategies, problem-solved challenging situations, and trained other staff members on how to effectively respond to and manage difficult behaviors. This experience helped establish my leadership skills and taught me the importance of staff development, consistency, and individualized support.

Over the years, I have continued to build on that foundation through my work as a Registered Behavior Technician. I have approximately four years of experience implementing behavior intervention plans, collecting and analyzing behavioral data, collaborating with BCBAs, and maintaining strong relationships with clients and their families. I have worked with children and adolescents with varying levels of behavioral and communication needs, including individuals who require significant support with emotional regulation and challenging behaviors.

Beyond my direct clinical experience, I consider myself a natural leader who values accountability, teamwork, and clear communication. I have experience training and guiding staff, modeling appropriate interventions, and helping others develop the skills and confidence needed to work effectively with challenging populations. I understand that successful programs depend on more than clinical services alone. They require organized daily operations, effective communication, staff coordination, accurate documentation, strong safety practices, and the ability to adapt when unexpected challenges arise.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to combine my behavioral health experience with my leadership abilities and passion for working with adolescents. While my background has primarily been in direct service, it has given me firsthand insight into the operational challenges staff face and the systems necessary to maintain a successful program. I am writing to express my interest in joining the Adolescent Wellness Academy team in Boca Raton. Your mission to provide adolescents with a safe, supportive environment where they feel seen, understood, and genuinely cared for deeply resonates with both my personal values and professional purpose.

As a board-certified Health and Wellness Coach, Hypnotherapist, and Fitness Instructor, I bring a holistic approach to physical, mental, and emotional well-being. My work focuses on helping individuals develop healthier habits, manage stress, build self-awareness, strengthen emotional resilience, and create positive, sustainable changes in their lives.

I strongly believe that the foundations of overall wellness should be taught from an early age. Equipping adolescents with practical tools for emotional regulation, stress management, mindfulness, healthy habits, and self-awareness can better prepare them to navigate the challenges of life and an increasingly demanding world. As a mother, I also appreciate the unique pressures adolescents face today and the importance of having compassionate, trustworthy individuals who can support and guide them through this formative stage of life.

I believe my background in health and mindset coaching, behavior change, mindfulness, breathwork, and nervous system regulation would complement AWA’s multidisciplinary approach. I bring warmth, empathy, patience, and a genuine passion for empowering others to recognize their potential and develop the skills to thrive.

What particularly draws me to AWA is your commitment to seeing beyond an adolescent’s struggles and recognizing the individual within. I would love the opportunity to collaborate with your team and contribute to an organization that shares my belief in nurturing the whole person.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications, experience, and passion for holistic well-being could contribute to your team and make a meaningful difference in the lives of the adolescents and families you serve.

Warm regards,

Christina Samuda

November 25, 2026

Hiring Team Adolescent Wellness Academy Boca Raton, FL

Re: Creative Group Facilitator – Adolescent Mental Health

Dear AWA Hiring Team,

I'm excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator role. I'm a K–8 art teacher with a B.A. in Studio Art and Psychology from Florida State University, and I'm currently earning my M.S. in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Walden University. I've spent my career at the point where art, behavior and emotional growth meet. Helping teens build confidence and coping skills through creative work is exactly the kind of work I want to be doing.

Leading groups with adolescents. 
I teach art to students in kindergarten through 8th grade, including middle schoolers on the edge of the age group AWA serves. Every day I plan and lead hands-on lessons that work for students with very different skill levels, attention spans and comfort with being creative in front of peers. I created a tiered behavior escalation framework for my classroom, so I can handle tough group moments calmly and consistently while keeping the room safe for everyone. After my first year, I built a full curriculum by hand, planned month by month so lessons build on each other and stay fresh.

Adapting creative work to each person. 
As a Clinical Educator at Cayer Behavioral Group, an ABA practice, I worked with K–5 children with autism. I used each child's data to design sensory-friendly, hands-on activities tailored to their needs. I worked alongside the clinical team and advocated for the kids, especially around their feelings. Earlier, as a nanny, I ran "Creative Play" sessions with short art lessons built into each child's care plan. I've learned that the activity is only the vehicle. What matters is whether each participant feels safe enough to try.

A clinical lens. 
My psychology coursework at FSU included abnormal psychology, neurodivergence and neuroscience. At Walden, I'm studying counseling techniques and trauma-informed care. In a PHP or IOP setting, that helps me understand what teens may be carrying into the room. It also helps me know when to invite expression and when to give space, and how to document what I see in a way that's useful to the clinical team. I'm used to timely documentation from tracking student progress data and keeping records in my school's gradebook system.

My own creative background goes beyond the classroom.
It includes studio art, commissioned signage work and clarinet performance, so I can offer a range of expressive activities, from drawing and collage to music and mindful making. I'd love to bring that range, along with real care for teens, to your village.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I'd welcome the chance to talk about how I could support AWA's creative programming.

Sincerely,

Justine Therrien

Shamaiah Manriquez
South Florida
331-250-1652
ShamaiahM@Gmail.com

October 28, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in joining the team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With hands-on experience in youth development, art instruction, creative education, and community programming, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to an environment dedicated to supporting adolescents’ well-being, personal development, and growth.

My experience working with children and teens through the Boys & Girls Club and the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp has strengthened my appreciation for the importance of creating positive, structured, and encouraging environments where young people can develop confidence, explore their strengths, and express themselves constructively. Through art instruction and guided creative workshops, I have facilitated activities that incorporate painting, storytelling, imagination, and self-expression to encourage creativity, personal growth, and meaningful engagement.

In 2025, I served as an art instructor for the Billy Thompson Foundation Youth Summer Camp, delivering structured art workshops for children and teenagers. I also led a community painting experience at JPP International Church through Painting With A Twist, facilitating an engaging group activity for approximately 40 participants. Earlier in my career, my work with the Boys & Girls Club involved youth art programming designed to encourage imagination, confidence, and self-expression. These experiences have reinforced my belief that young people benefit from opportunities to discover their abilities, develop positive relationships, and engage in activities that promote healthy self-expression.

I currently serve as Program Coordinator for Paint With Purpose, a community arts and creative wellness initiative that uses guided painting experiences to encourage self-expression, confidence, healing, and connection. My responsibilities include developing and coordinating creative workshops, planning activities, preparing materials, communicating with participants, and exploring partnerships with community organizations and schools. This work reflects my commitment to using creativity as a constructive way to bring people together and create meaningful community experiences.

In addition to my experience in youth programming and the arts, I bring more than 10 years of experience in administrative support, client relations, organizational coordination, and professional communication. My background includes supporting leadership, coordinating schedules and activities, managing documentation, and handling confidential information with discretion. These skills would allow me to contribute organization, reliability, professionalism, and effective communication to your team.

I am also pursuing a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology at South Florida Bible College, with anticipated completion in 2028. My educational path complements my interest in human development, individual strengths, and the factors that contribute to personal growth and well-being. As an artist, published children’s book author, and creative educator, I am passionate about helping people recognize their potential and discover constructive ways to communicate and express themselves. My CPR and AED certification, obtained in 2023, further reflects my commitment to maintaining relevant practical skills.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, creativity, compassion, and organizational strengths to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am particularly interested in contributing to a supportive environment where adolescents are encouraged to develop healthy coping strategies, build confidence, strengthen interpersonal skills, and recognize their capacity for growth. I would be proud to contribute to a team that approaches youth development with professionalism, respect, consistency, and an understanding of the importance of individualized support.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in youth development, creative programming, psychology studies, and professional administration could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and its mission.

Sincerely,

Shamaiah Manriquez

10/27/2026
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy,
I am writing to express my interest in the Adolescent Mental Health Therapist position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Registered Clinical Social Work Intern with an MSW from Florida Atlantic University, I am dedicated to working alongside vulnerable children and families, and I would welcome the chance to bring my hands-on clinical experience and my commitment to growth to your team.
In my current role as Family Advocate / Clinical Case Manager at CityHouse, I deliver crisis intervention, de-escalation, and stabilization services, conduct comprehensive psychosocial and needs assessments with resident families, and provide counseling to children and families using evidence-based, trauma-informed interventions. I develop individualized treatment plans with measurable goals in collaboration with clients and the clinical team, then monitor progress and adjust plans as needs change. I also assisted in developing a children's therapeutic service program and an intentional therapeutic room across two campuses, a space designed so children feel safe and supported.
My MSW internship at CityHouse deepened my work with children and their caregivers. I created and facilitated an 8-week social-emotional learning group for children ages 8-12, and I advocated for IEP and educational needs for elementary-aged children, supporting mothers at parent-teacher conferences. Earlier, as a BSW intern and Behavioral Technician at Aces for Autism, I provided 1:1 applied behavior analysis sessions for children, including children with autism spectrum disorder, and completed clinical documentation. Together, these experiences taught me to meet each family where they are and build on their strengths.
What draws me to social work is the opportunity to walk alongside children and families through difficult moments and help them recognize their own strengths. I am currently accruing clinical hours toward LCSW licensure in Florida, and I am committed to ongoing growth through supervision, training, and hands-on practice.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how I can contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy, and I can be reached at 845-600-5746 or accurson02@yahoo.com.
Sincerely,
Nadia Accurso, MSW Registered Clinical Social Work Intern

Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI #29711) and behavioral health professional with 7+ years of experience across mental health, substance use treatment, crisis intervention, case management, child welfare, and criminal justice settings. I hold Master’s degrees in Clinical Mental Health Counseling and Human Services.

My experience includes outpatient counseling, Medication-Assisted Treatment (MAT), admissions and intake, biopsychosocial and risk assessments, treatment planning, individual and group counseling, crisis intervention, and care coordination. I utilize trauma-informed care, Motivational Interviewing, CBT, and person-centered approaches when working with diverse and complex populations.

I bring a unique combination of clinical expertise, human services experience, and systems knowledge and am committed to continued growth within behavioral health, clinical services, care coordination, and program leadership.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I am especially drawn to AWA Academy because of the impact your work has on the lives of children and families, and I would love to be part of that mission.

I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. I also have experience working in an inpatient psychiatric hospital with adults, where I facilitated group therapy and conducted intake assessments. These experiences have helped me build my clinical skills, connect with clients from different backgrounds, and better understand the importance of compassionate, individualized care.

Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. Working with children and families was one of the most meaningful parts of my professional journey and played a big role in shaping the kind of therapist I wanted to become. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. I would love the opportunity to bring that passion into my clinical work with adolescents and their families.

My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I am eager to learn, grow, and challenge myself as a clinician, and I would be grateful for the opportunity to do so alongside a team that shares my commitment to supporting young people through difficult moments in their lives.

I am also fluent in both English and Portuguese, which allows me to connect with and support families from different linguistic and cultural backgrounds. I currently hold a license as a Registered Mental Health Intern and have a qualified supervisor. I anticipate to become fully licensed in a year and a half.

I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Thank you!

Rebecca Ubertini

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Therapy position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Registered Clinical Social Work Intern (RCSWI), I am passionate about supporting individuals through life’s challenges and helping them develop the tools and skills necessary to achieve emotional wellness, resilience, and personal growth. I believe my clinical experience, diverse background working with various populations, and dedication to providing compassionate, client-centered care would make me a valuable addition to your team.

In my current role, I provide therapeutic services to youth, adolescents, and adults with a wide range of mental health and behavioral health needs, including PTSD, depression, anxiety, ADHD, autism, and substance use disorders. I utilize evidence-based therapeutic approaches, including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), and trauma-informed care, to help clients navigate challenges, strengthen coping skills, regulate emotions, and work toward their individualized treatment goals. I strive to create a safe, supportive, and nonjudgmental therapeutic environment where clients feel heard, respected, and empowered throughout their healing journey.

In addition to my clinical experience, I have worked with diverse and vulnerable populations, including individuals impacted by domestic violence, substance use, homelessness, disabilities, and challenges associated with aging. These experiences have strengthened my ability to approach each individual with empathy, patience, cultural sensitivity, and an understanding of the unique circumstances that influence mental health and overall well-being. I recognize the importance of meeting clients where they are, building trusting therapeutic relationships, and tailoring interventions to their individual needs and strengths.

I am a driven, hardworking, compassionate, and dedicated professional who values collaboration, continued learning, and professional growth. I am committed to helping clients recognize their strengths, overcome barriers, and build healthier, more fulfilling lives. I am particularly interested in the opportunity to contribute my skills and passion to Adolescent Wellness Academy and support the emotional and psychological well-being of the individuals and families served by your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical experience, therapeutic approach, and commitment to quality mental health care align with the needs of your team. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to the important work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Ryan Blanchette
Sioux Falls, SD 57105 | (605) 370-9495 | artorius009@gmail.com
November 23, 2026
Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Dear Hiring Team,
I applied today for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position and wanted to share a little more about my background.
For nine years I worked in intensive residential treatment programs in Minnesota, supporting adults living with mental illness and, often, substance use. I helped clients build relapse prevention plans and led DBT skills and Illness Management and Recovery groups under clinical supervision. I completed discharge summaries, helped people transition to their next placement, and kept in touch with outside agencies so their care stayed consistent. I understand what a structured level of care offers someone, and I can explain it to a worried parent in plain language.
Many of the people who call you are having one of the hardest days of their lives. In residential treatment, I worked with people through mental health crises and relapses, often when they were scared or overwhelmed. I know how to stay calm, listen first, and still guide the conversation toward a clear next step.
I also bring the practical side of intake. At Sanford Health Ophthalmology, I took patient histories and managed scheduling and demographic records in medical software. As a former licensed insurance agent in South Dakota, I am comfortable talking through coverage and benefits. At Sioux Falls Ford, I was each customer's point of contact from check-in to completion, and I followed up until every job was done.
I work well on my own and keep careful records. I would welcome the chance to talk with you about helping families get from that first call to their first day of care.
Thank you for your time.
Sincerely,
Ryan Blanchette

Compassionate Healthcare & HIPAA Experience: Serving as a Certified Nurse Aide (CNA) at the Claremore Veterans Center (VA) from January through August, I provided empathetic daily care, listened actively to patient and family concerns, and documented confidential records in full compliance with HIPAA standards.

Remote Readiness & Administrative Precision: Experienced with CRM systems, Microsoft Office, Google Suite, and structured data entry, I excel in independent, deadline-driven workflows and take pride in thorough, organized follow-up.
Holding an Associate of Science degree from Tulsa Community College and fluency in English and Hmong (with conversational Spanish), I am dedicated to making every family feel heard, respected, and supported from their very first call or inquiry. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my healthcare background, organizational discipline, and compassionate communication skills to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Andrew Thao

I am excited to express my interest in joining the Adolescent Wellness Academy team. My background in psychology, education, youth development, and counseling has given me a strong appreciation for the importance of providing adolescents with a safe and supportive environment where they feel heard, understood, and encouraged to grow. I earned my bachelor’s degree in Psychology from the University of Georgia and am currently pursuing my master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Walden University. My long-term goal is to work with adolescents experiencing mental health challenges, particularly young people who face additional barriers to accessing support and resources.

Throughout my career, I have worked with young people in several capacities, including as a middle school science teacher, a Teacher Counselor with Youth Villages, and an Educational Specialist with the TRIO Upward Bound program. These experiences taught me how important it is to build trust, communicate effectively, recognize individual needs, and meet young people where they are. I have also developed experience supporting students through academic, behavioral, and personal challenges while collaborating with families, educators, and other professionals. What interests me about Adolescent Wellness Academy is its commitment to looking beyond symptoms and creating a community where adolescents and their families can experience meaningful growth. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, perspective, and passion for working with young people to your team. Thank you for your time and consideration. Sincerely,
Francis Macharia

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Master's degree in Healthcare Management, a Bachelor's degree in Collaborative Health and Human Services, and a professional background in healthcare administration, patient coordination, and advocacy, I believe I bring a valuable combination of organizational skills, compassionate communication, and a genuine commitment to helping individuals and families navigate challenging circumstances.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed a strong foundation in coordinating services, communicating with individuals from diverse backgrounds, and helping people navigate systems that can often feel overwhelming. My background in medical assisting and surgery scheduling has provided me with experience independently managing patient scheduling, coordinating appointments, handling insurance-related responsibilities, managing sensitive information, and communicating with patients and healthcare professionals. These experiences have strengthened my ability to remain organized, detail-oriented, and compassionate while managing multiple priorities and responsibilities independently.

Additionally, my experience in domestic violence advocacy has been particularly meaningful in shaping my approach to supporting individuals and families during difficult periods in their lives. Through advocacy services and support group involvement, I gained experience in active listening, recognizing individual needs, connecting people with appropriate resources, and providing judgment-free support. I understand the importance of approaching sensitive conversations with empathy, patience, and professionalism, especially when individuals are seeking help during vulnerable moments.

My previous experience as a Student Assistant in the Admissions Office at California State University, Monterey Bay, also provided me with valuable experience guiding prospective students and their families through the admissions process. I assisted with inquiries, communicated university requirements and processes, and helped connect families with the appropriate resources. This experience strengthened my ability to make unfamiliar processes easier to understand and help individuals feel supported when making important decisions.

I recognize that my resume reflects an employment gap over the past two and a half years, during which I made the intentional decision to step away from my professional career to focus on raising my son during his early childhood. This was an important and rewarding chapter of my life, and I am now excited and ready to return to the workforce. I look forward to bringing my education, previous professional experience, and renewed enthusiasm to an organization where I can make a meaningful difference. I am also excited about the opportunity to transition my administrative and coordination experience into a remote environment, where I can continue providing dependable, professional, and compassionate support.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because of the chance to be a supportive first point of contact for individuals and families seeking care. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming step, and I would take great pride in helping make that process feel more approachable, organized, and compassionate. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my background in healthcare administration, advocacy, and client coordination to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, education, and passion for helping others align with the needs of your organization.

Sincerely,

Brianna Klingelhoets

Hiring Team:

Remote
To whom it may concern,
I found your job posting on Indeed during my job search tonight and knew right away I am a strong fit for the position. I have directly worked with at-risk youth at the Charleston Job Corps, some of whom struggled with addiction. My last job was telecommunications-related, so I’m a quick starter. But more importantly, I have been through recovery, so I know firsthand what that’s about. I’ve been sober for almost 15 years. 

I have also raised two children. One works for Toyota, and the other is in her second year in college. Family is the most important thing, and maintaining it with inclusive communication practices can increase one’s success in recovery. I bring my lived experience with me as a candidate, as well as my educational and professional background.

My work history also makes me a strong fit for the role: At Foundever, I handled calls full-time; active listening, empathy, and a strong commitment to ethics were essential to the role of frontline agent. I always maintained high CSAT scores (in the high 90s), and I never fell prey to social engineering. Protecting personally identifiable information was always the highest priority. 

My average handle time was around 353 seconds with some deviation. In my experience, efficient call-taking increases both speed and accuracy, but people also need kindness when their lives are falling apart and they are on the razor’s edge. Many people have helped me along the way, and I would be honored to help someone else in return.

Thank you so much for your time and any consideration you give to my application.

Respectfully,
Bryan K. Sparks

candidates.summary:
Firstly, I worked as an in-home healthcare worker for roughly 2.5 years; there, I cared for someone with intellectual and developmental disabilities, and I was AMAP-certified. As an AMAP, I worked with registered nurses to assist the client through a medical model, while the behavioral program was largely cognitive-behavioral. My job was to help the client be as independent as possible while observing their behavior and administering medications (both on a schedule and as needed). 

Secondly, I worked for MTC at the Charleston Job Corps with at-risk youth ages 16 to 24 as their residential advisor. As an RA, I helped to keep order; moreover, I kept a log of egress and ingress, assisted students with their medications, conducted room checks, and reported instances of misconduct to security and senior staff. RAs also mentor students and serve as role models.

Lastly, I was a frontline agent on behalf of a major credit card company. I had to familiarize myself with telecommunications law and refamiliarize myself with aspects of GAAP, all while being sensitive to the client's vision for the company, being aware of the role that customer service plays in their business model, and handling sensitive data in a highly volatile communicative environment. Often, however, customers want someone to take them seriously and to listen, and I tried very hard to make each customer feel appreciated, heard, and completely safe--while serving the business interests of the client and its customers.

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a Bachelor’s degree in Pre-Medical Sciences, ongoing education in healthcare administration, and previous professional experience in customer service and fast-paced work environments, I am eager to contribute to an organization dedicated to supporting adolescents and their families.

Mental health awareness and patient advocacy are areas that are particularly meaningful to me. I understand that seeking mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming and emotional experience for both adolescents and their loved ones. I believe that having someone who listens with empathy, communicates clearly, and provides guidance without judgment can make a significant difference in their healthcare journey.

My previous employment with Walt Disney World and Amazon helped me develop strong communication, organization, time management, problem-solving, and teamwork skills. Additionally, my healthcare-related education has provided me with a foundation in medical terminology and healthcare practices.

As a bilingual professional fluent in English and Spanish, I would welcome the opportunity to help reduce communication barriers and assist families from diverse backgrounds. I am comfortable learning new systems, managing multiple responsibilities, and handling sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.

Although I am transitioning into healthcare administration, I bring a genuine passion for helping others, a strong willingness to learn, and a commitment to providing compassionate and reliable support.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s mission and help families take the first steps toward receiving the care and support they need.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss my qualifications further.

Sincerely,

Jessie Burgos Gonzalez

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

Thank you for the opportunity to provide additional information regarding my application for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am excited about the possibility of joining your team and contributing to an organization dedicated to helping adolescents and families navigate mental health and substance use treatment.

My career has been dedicated to helping others, advocating for their needs, and making a meaningful difference in their lives. With 13 years of experience as a Certified Nursing Assistant, I have had the privilege of working with individuals across various age groups and care settings, including hospitals, rehabilitation centers specializing in injury recovery, home health, and mental health care. These experiences have strengthened my ability to approach individuals with compassion, patience, empathy, and an understanding that every person’s circumstances and needs are different.

In addition to my direct patient care experience, I bring a strong background in healthcare administration and patient access. Through my work with Atlantic Health, Ascension, and Hummingbird Healthcare, I have developed experience in patient scheduling, referral coordination, medication refill requests, patient portal assistance, and virtual patient support. I am comfortable communicating with patients and families, managing sensitive information, navigating electronic medical record systems, and helping individuals work through what can sometimes be overwhelming healthcare processes. I understand the importance of listening, building trust, providing clear information, and ensuring that people feel supported rather than rushed or overlooked.

What particularly interests me about Adolescent Wellness Academy is the opportunity to support adolescents during a critical and often challenging stage of life. I believe young people deserve to feel heard, valued, and supported, especially when navigating mental health challenges. My passion for this population also extends beyond my professional responsibilities. One of my long-term goals is to establish a teen mentoring program within my community that provides young people with encouragement, guidance, positive relationships, and access to resources that can help them build confidence and navigate life’s challenges.

I believe I would be a strong addition to your team because I offer a unique combination of hands-on healthcare experience, patient access knowledge, strong communication skills, and a genuine commitment to helping others. I recognize that an admissions coordinator is often one of the first points of contact for families seeking help, and I would approach that responsibility with compassion, professionalism, sensitivity, and a commitment to making each interaction meaningful.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, dedication, and passion for patient advocacy align with the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy. I look forward to the possibility of contributing to your team.

Warm regards,

Jakyia Etienne

November 24, 2026

Dear Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

What drew me to this role was the opportunity to be the first person someone speaks to when they decide they need help. I understand that many of those calls happen on some of the hardest days of a person's life, and I believe my background has prepared me well for those conversations.

For six years, I worked in Emergency Medical Services, responding to people during medical emergencies, mental health crises, and situations involving individuals experiencing severe emotional distress. During that time, I learned how to remain calm under pressure, listen without judgment, communicate clearly, and help people navigate difficult circumstances. Some of the most important moments weren't medical at all. They were simply being able to connect with someone, earn their trust, and help them take the next step.

After EMS, I went on to build and operate my own restaurant business. Owning a business taught me how to manage people, solve problems, stay organized, and communicate with individuals from every walk of life. Whether helping a customer, supporting an employee, or resolving a difficult situation, I found that my greatest strength has always been working with people.

I am not applying because I am looking for just another job. I'm applying because this is one of the few opportunities I've come across that genuinely interests me. Helping people find resources, treatment, and support during difficult periods of their lives is meaningful work, and I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience and background can contribute to the important work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

James Theodoredis

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am interested in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I have a master's degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Florida Gulf Coast University and over 10 years of experience helping individuals and families with a variety of needs.

Throughout my career, I have worked with children and adults experiencing mental health challenges, substance use disorders, and developmental disabilities. During my time as a Substance Abuse Counselor and Case Manager at Charlotte Behavioral Health Care, I conducted assessments, developed treatment plans, and worked with other professionals to ensure clients received the services they needed. I also worked as a Mental Health Therapist at Life Share, providing counseling to both children and adults.

My experience as a Disaster Case Manager at Endeavors has given me the opportunity to help individuals and families navigate difficult situations. My responsibilities included conducting intakes, determining eligibility, connecting clients with resources, following up with clients, and maintaining accurate documentation.

One of the reasons I am interested in this position is because I enjoy connecting people with resources that can improve their quality of life. The reality is that asking for help can be difficult, especially when someone doesn't know where to turn. I believe it's important to make people feel heard, respected, and supported throughout that process. Even if we are unable to provide the services someone needs, we can still help them find the resources that are right for them.

I believe my education, experience, and passion for helping others would allow me to make a positive contribution to your organization. I also believe there is always room to learn and grow as a professional.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I look forward to the opportunity to speak with you.

Sincerely,

Shawn Hetz

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I bring along a Bachelor of Science in Biology, with minors in Psychology and Chemistry. To accompany this I bring my hands-on behavioral health experience as a Registered Behavior Technician, and a strong background in patient care and customer service, I believe I would bring a valuable combination of compassion, empathy, professionalism, and organizational skills to your admissions team.

In my current role as a Registered Behavior Technician with Attain ABA, I work directly with children with autism and developmental delays, providing individualized support while following established treatment plans. This experience has strengthened my ability to build trust, communicate with families, recognize individual needs, maintain accurate documentation, and approach sensitive situations with patience and empathy. I understand how important it is for individuals and families to feel heard, respected, and supported when navigating behavioral health services.

My previous experience as an Ophthalmic Technician at Sewickley Eye Group further developed my healthcare communication and administrative skills. I regularly collected patient medical histories, documented chief complaints, prepared patients for examinations, and communicated important information to healthcare providers. Additionally, my experience in customer-facing roles has taught me how to manage competing priorities, respond to questions and concerns, and provide professional, solutions-oriented assistance in fast-paced environments.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the chance to make a meaningful difference before treatment even begins. I recognize that families seeking mental health or substance use treatment may be experiencing uncertainty, fear, and emotional stress. I would approach my role with genuine commitment to helping callers understand their options and take the next step toward receiving care.

I am bilingual in English and Spanish, comfortable working with sensitive information, and experienced in maintaining accurate records while following established procedures. I am also eager to expand my experience with admissions coordination, insurance verification, and electronic medical record systems. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my behavioral health knowledge, healthcare experience, and dedication to patient-centered service to your organization.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background, skills, and passion for helping individuals and families could contribute to your admissions team. I look forward to the possibility of joining your organization and helping people take the first step toward healing.

Sincerely,
Countess Lily Vason

candidates.cover_letter:
Hello, 
I hope you will read this. 

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. After reading the job description, I felt a genuine connection to the role because it combines my healthcare experience with something that is personally important to me: helping people who may be going through some of the hardest moments in their lives.

I currently work for Quest Diagnostics, where I work with patients, healthcare providers, and medical offices on a daily basis. My responsibilities include answering questions, processing payments, collecting insurance information, coordinating appointments, handling lab orders and paperwork, and making sure everything is completed accurately and in a timely manner. This experience has helped me develop strong communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills while teaching me the importance of patience and understanding when working with others.

On a more personal level, I understand what it feels like to be someone who needs help. I know that reaching out for support isn’t always easy, and sometimes that first conversation can make a bigger difference than people realize. Having personally experienced the need for support, I have an understanding of how important it is to feel heard, respected, and not judged. Sometimes people aren’t sure what to say, where to start, or even how to ask for help. I believe the way someone is treated during that first interaction can have a lasting impact on whether they feel comfortable taking that next step.

That is one of the biggest reasons this position stands out to me. I would genuinely enjoy being a welcoming voice for someone who may be nervous, overwhelmed, or unsure of what comes next. I want people to feel like they are talking to someone who cares, not just someone answering a phone and going through a checklist.

I would bring my healthcare experience, dependability, attention to detail, and, most importantly, a genuine understanding of how much compassion and kindness matter when someone is seeking help. I would love the opportunity to be part of a team that makes a difference for individuals and families who need it.

Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would truly appreciate the opportunity to speak with you and learn more about becoming part of your team.

Sincerely, annnd thank you, 

Martika

Dear Hiring Team,
I am writing to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. The idea of being the first voice someone hears on a hard day is one I take seriously, and my background in listening, de-escalation, and dependable follow-through is what I would bring to that role.

Earlier, as an Assistant Manager and Certified Trainer at Buffalo Wild Wings, I supervised a team of 15 or more, mediated conflicts, and handled grievances with fairness.
My degree in Sociology with a minor in Psychology from Midwestern State University gives me a solid understanding of human behavior and of how people communicate under stress. During my HR internship with the City of Wichita Falls, I handled confidential employee matters with discretion and followed HR ethical standards, and I received formal recognition from the City Manager for my work on employee surveys. That experience taught me to treat sensitive information carefully, which I know matters in a HIPAA-compliant admissions setting.
I am comfortable with Microsoft Office and customer relationship management, and I am quick to learn new systems. I should be upfront that my background is in customer service and human resources rather than behavioral health admissions, but I am committed to learning your programs, insurance verification process, and intake workflow. I am a careful record-keeper who follows up until each person has a clear next step.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can support your admissions team and the families you serve.
Sincerely, Eric McManus

PHOEBEE JEAN-JACQUES
Naples, FL
239-351-8777 | ietangel0687@yahoo.com
November 25, 2026
Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy / Principles Recovery Center
RE: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With over seven years of progressive professional experience, including direct experience in behavioral health, healthcare services, remote client intake, and confidential information management, I believe my background aligns well with the responsibilities and compassionate approach required for this position.
My experience at David Lawrence Centers, where I served as a Behavioral Health Technician, Admission and Intake for the Detox and Mental Health facilities, then as a Human Resources Coordinator for more than five years, provided me with valuable exposure to the behavioral health environment and the importance of supporting an organization dedicated to mental and substance abuse health services. Additionally, my experience as an Intake Specialist in a detoxification setting strengthened my understanding of the intake process and the sensitivity required when working with individuals navigating challenging personal circumstances.
In my previous remote position as an Intake Contact Caller with A Case For Women, I managed a high volume of inbound and outbound communications, conducted detailed intake conversations, gathered sensitive information, answer questions, and guided individuals through the next steps of the process. I am responsible for maintaining accurate client records in a CRM, following up consistently, and ensuring that each individual feels heard, respected, and supported. Working remotely has also strengthened my ability to manage my responsibilities independently, prioritize my workload, and maintain productivity without constant supervision.
Furthermore, my experience as a Video Remote Interpreter with AMN Healthcare has strengthened my ability to communicate effectively in sensitive healthcare settings while maintaining confidentiality, professionalism, and accuracy. As a fluent speaker of English, French, and Haitian Creole, I bring an additional ability to connect with individuals and families from diverse backgrounds and help bridge communication barriers.
What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to make a meaningful difference at the very beginning of someone's treatment journey. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming and emotional experience, especially for families seeking help for their children. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my intake experience, behavioral health exposure, communication skills, and genuine compassion to a team that helps individuals and families take that important first step toward healing.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my professional background and commitment to compassionate client support could contribute to the continued success of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I look forward to hearing from you.
Sincerely,
Phoebee Jean-Jacques

candidates.cover_letter:
When I was 17, I entered an intensive inpatient program for substance use and spent 18 months there. That program saved my life. Today I’m 18 years sober, and I still remember how frightening it was to walk through those doors. I also understand how hard it can be to make that first call when it’s someone you love who needs help. I’m applying to be a Virtual Admissions Coordinator because I want to answer that call with warmth and give the person on the other end time to find the words.

I worked remotely for the Culinary Careers Program (C·CAP) for more than four years. One of my favorite parts of the job was helping high school students through the scholarship process. I prepared finalist packets and coordinated interviews with college partners, making sure students and program staff had the dates and details they needed. I also kept Salesforce records current so colleagues in different regions could see whom we had contacted and who was waiting for a response.

At SAIC, I guided new staff through onboarding for an FAA training program. I handled sensitive personnel documents and followed up on missing paperwork so people could get the approvals they needed to start work. Earlier, as a reporter covering LGBTQ youth homelessness, I interviewed advocates about where teens could go when shelters were full. Those conversations taught me to ask difficult questions plainly and give people time to answer.

A parent calling Adolescent Wellness Academy might want to know whether their child can keep up with school during treatment. An adult reaching out to Principles Recovery Center might be trying to plan around work. I’d start with that concern and explain what a week in partial hospitalization or intensive outpatient care looks like. From there, I’d help verify coverage and schedule an assessment. If another provider were a better fit, I’d follow up to see whether the caller had been able to reach them.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the chance to speak with you about joining your admissions team.

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a strong educational background in psychology and professional experience in mental health counseling, substance use treatment, adolescent behavioral health, and case management, I believe my qualifications and passion for helping others align closely with the mission of your programs.

Throughout my career, I have worked with children, adolescents, and adults experiencing a wide range of mental health challenges, substance use disorders, and co-occurring conditions. My professional experience includes individual and group counseling, psychosocial assessments, treatment planning, crisis intervention, care coordination, and connecting individuals and families with appropriate resources. My experience in substance use treatment has also provided me with a strong understanding of ASAM criteria, individualized treatment needs, and the importance of connecting individuals with the appropriate level of care.

I understand that reaching out for treatment can be one of the most difficult and vulnerable steps an individual or family takes. I take pride in my ability to establish rapport, communicate with empathy, and create a supportive, nonjudgmental environment in which individuals feel heard, respected, and understood. I recognize that an admissions coordinator is often the first point of contact for someone seeking treatment, and that this initial interaction can significantly influence their willingness to move forward with care.

In addition to my clinical experience, I possess strong organizational, communication, and time-management skills. I am experienced in managing substantial caseloads, maintaining accurate electronic health records, coordinating services with multidisciplinary teams, and adhering to HIPAA and professional confidentiality standards. I am comfortable working independently, managing competing priorities, learning new software systems, and maintaining consistent follow-through without requiring constant supervision.

My academic background includes a Bachelor of Arts in Psychology with a concentration in Forensic Psychology and minors in Sociology and Criminal Justice, as well as graduate-level education in Forensic Psychology through Southern New Hampshire University. My education and professional experience have strengthened my understanding of trauma-informed care, behavioral health, addiction, and the barriers individuals often encounter when seeking treatment.

What particularly draws me to this opportunity is the ability to make a meaningful difference at the very beginning of someone's recovery journey. I believe that accessing mental health and substance use treatment should be a compassionate, supportive, and straightforward process. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my clinical knowledge, interpersonal skills, and genuine commitment to helping others to both Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to further discuss how my experience, education, and dedication to behavioral health would make me a valuable addition to your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Alexandria Tobin

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a background in healthcare outreach, patient access, insurance verification, and customer service, I believe I bring a valuable combination of administrative experience, communication skills, and compassion that would make me a strong addition to your team.

In my current role as an Outreach Specialist with Blue Birds Kids Health, I work with parents and families to assist with new patient registration, insurance verification, appointment scheduling, and patient communication. I also use Athenahealth and Talkdesk to manage patient information, document interactions, and coordinate follow-ups. Working in a hybrid position has helped me become comfortable balancing in-office and remote responsibilities while staying organized, productive, and independent.

Before entering healthcare, I gained several years of experience in fine dining and hospitality. Those experiences taught me how important it is to listen, communicate effectively, be patient, and make people feel comfortable and welcomed. I have learned how to remain calm under pressure, handle different situations with professionalism, and give people my full attention.

What really draws me to this position is the opportunity to make a difference in the lives of individuals and families who may be going through a difficult time. I genuinely care about helping others and understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be a big and sometimes overwhelming step. I also recognize the responsibility of being the first person someone speaks to during that time, and I would never take that lightly. I would want every caller to feel heard, respected, and supported, knowing they are speaking with someone who truly cares and wants to make that first interaction a little easier.

I would love the opportunity to bring my healthcare experience, communication skills, and willingness to learn to your team. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I look forward to the possibility of speaking with you!

Sincerely,

Gabriella Sheen

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With over 10 years of experience in behavioral health, substance use treatment, psychiatric care, crisis intervention, and case management, I bring a strong clinical background and a genuine commitment to helping individuals and families navigate the treatment process.

In my current work with New Directions Treatment Services and Creative Health Services, I support individuals experiencing substance use disorders and co-occurring mental health conditions. My responsibilities include assessing client needs, coordinating treatment services, maintaining accurate clinical documentation, communicating with referral sources, and helping clients overcome barriers to care.

My previous experience with Pottstown Hospital–Tower Health also provided opportunities to assist with insurance authorization and precertification processes, including communicating with insurance companies to help clients obtain approval for appropriate levels of care. Additionally, my background working with adolescents and families has strengthened my ability to establish rapport, navigate sensitive conversations, and provide compassionate guidance during challenging circumstances.

I understand that reaching out for behavioral health treatment can be overwhelming for both individuals and their loved ones. My counseling experience has equipped me with the active listening, motivational interviewing, problem-solving, and interpersonal communication skills necessary to make those initial conversations supportive, informative, and productive.

I am comfortable managing competing priorities, maintaining confidential electronic clinical records, working independently, and following through on client needs. I am confident that my clinical knowledge and care coordination experience would translate effectively into screening prospective clients, coordinating assessments and admissions, supporting insurance verification, and connecting families with appropriate treatment services.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it allows me to combine my behavioral health experience with admissions coordination and client advocacy while supporting both adolescent and adult populations.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, professionalism, and commitment to compassionate care can contribute to the continued success of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

Shakeem M. Tomlin

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with your organization. I am excited about the opportunity to combine my administrative and organizational skills with my passion for helping individuals and families access the care and support they need.

I bring 10 years of hands-on caregiving experience in assisted living and memory care facilities in Colorado. Throughout those years, I developed a strong understanding of the importance of patience, compassion, communication, and treating every individual with dignity and respect. Working closely with residents and their families has taught me how important it is to listen, understand individual needs, provide reassurance, and remain professional during difficult or emotional situations.

My caregiving background, combined with my office and administrative experience, has helped me develop strong communication, organization, multitasking, and problem-solving skills. I understand the importance of confidentiality, accurate documentation, and creating a welcoming and supportive experience for individuals and families.

I recognize that seeking mental health or substance use treatment for an adolescent can be an overwhelming and emotional experience for both the individual and their family. I would take pride in being a compassionate and understanding first point of contact, helping families navigate the admissions process and connect with the resources and treatment they need.

I am dependable, adaptable, comfortable learning new systems, and capable of working independently while maintaining effective communication with a team. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my 10 years of caregiving experience, administrative abilities, and genuine desire to help others to your admissions department.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience, skills, and passion for helping others could make me a valuable addition to your team.

Sincerely,

Rachel McGlochlin

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a diverse background in healthcare, medical coding, and childcare, I am eager to transition into a role that allows me to combine my administrative skills with my passion for helping individuals and families.

My healthcare experience has provided me with a strong understanding of medical terminology, patient confidentiality, HIPAA compliance, and the importance of accurate documentation. Additionally, my previous experience working remotely as a medical coder has strengthened my ability to work independently, stay organized, manage responsibilities, and learn new systems.

Through my experience working with children and families, I have developed strong communication skills, patience, empathy, and the ability to approach sensitive situations with compassion and understanding. I recognize how overwhelming it can be for families to navigate healthcare decisions, especially when seeking mental health or substance use treatment for their children.

While my professional background has not been directly within behavioral health admissions, I am eager to learn and confident that my transferable skills would allow me to become a valuable member of your team.

At this stage in my career, I am intentionally seeking a long-term opportunity where I can grow professionally, contribute to a meaningful mission, and make a positive difference in the lives of others. The opportunity to support families during some of their most vulnerable moments is something I would find incredibly fulfilling.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background, dedication, and willingness to learn could contribute to your team.

Sincerely,

Josi Lins

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position focused on adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. As a Master of Social Work student at Arizona State University with a background in public health and family support services, I am passionate about helping individuals and families access the resources they need during some of the most challenging moments in their lives.

My professional experience has centered on education, advocacy, outreach, and connecting people to essential services. During my time with Greenway Family Success Center, I worked directly with families to identify needs, develop action plans, and connect them with resources including healthcare, housing, employment assistance, and mental health supports. I also helped implement a community-wide mental health initiative designed to increase awareness and access to behavioral health resources. These experiences strengthened my ability to communicate with empathy, build rapport quickly, and guide individuals through complex decision-making processes.

In addition, as the founder of Cross-Cultural Education Services, I have managed client relationships from initial inquiry through ongoing engagement. This role has required strong organizational skills, consistent follow-up, effective communication, and the ability to understand each client's unique goals and circumstances. I am comfortable conducting conversations by phone, maintaining accurate records, coordinating schedules, and ensuring every client feels heard and supported.

What draws me most to this position is the opportunity to work with adolescents and families seeking mental health and substance use treatment. I understand that the first conversation a family has with an organization can significantly impact whether they pursue care. I would be honored to serve as a compassionate, knowledgeable first point of contact, helping families feel understood while guiding them toward appropriate treatment options.

Thank you for your consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in public health, family support, and social work can contribute to your team and the families you serve.

Sincerely,

Lauren Freeman

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I was
drawn to this role because the work matters at a very human level: for an adolescent and their family, the first
step toward mental health or substance use treatment is often a difficult phone call, made at a frightening moment. I would be proud to be a calm, clear, and kind first voice on that call, and the opportunity to do this work from home in Roswell makes it a strong fit.
From 2022 to 2026, I worked at Carnival Cruise Line in Resolutions and Executive Resolutions, most
recently as a Resolutions Coach training and developing a team of 20 or more agents who handled complex
and escalated concerns. The people contacting us were often upset, confused, or overwhelmed. My job was to slow the conversation down, listen carefully, explain options in plain language, de-escalate when needed,
and own each case through to resolution - with accurate documentation and follow-up in the CRM system.
Those are the habits I would bring to admissions: steady phone work, empathy without losing clarity, and no
loose ends for a family waiting on next steps.
I also bring lived experience in recovery. I share that briefly because I believe it is relevant here: I
understand, from the inside, that reaching out for help can involve fear and shame as well as hope, and that
how a person is treated in that first conversation can shape whether they follow through. I approach people
without judgment and with patience. I am also Mental Health First Responder certified, which has
strengthened how I recognize distress, respond calmly, and help connect people to support.
I am experienced working remotely and self-directedly. At Carnival I coached and presented virtually,
managed case documentation in Oracle and Salesforce, and was trusted with high-priority cases requiring strong judgment and accuracy. Since June 2025 I have also owned and operated a small business in Roswell, handling scheduling, customer communication, and operations on my own. I am comfortable learning new systems, following a process exactly, and handling sensitive information with care, all essential when intake
details affect a young person's care.
I want to be upfront that I do not have direct admissions experience in behavioral health. What I do have is
closely transferable experience, high-volume phone work, de-escalation, service recovery, case ownership,
documentation, and follow-through - together with lived recovery experience and a genuine commitment to this kind of work. I am eager to learn your intake process and standards.
Thank you for your consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to speak with you about how my
background could support the adolescents and families who reach out to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

candidates.cover_letter:
Christina Worley
BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION & MANAGEMENT
819 S. 22nd St., Unionville, MO 63565 

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to apply for the Admissions Coordinator position in adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. I bring more than 10 years of management and more than 15 years of customer service experience in business administration, including medical customer service, healthcare billing, and long-term care. That combination — careful billing and record-keeping, direct work with patients and families, and calm, organized coordination — is the work at the heart of admissions, where a family's first experience of a program often comes at a very hard moment in their lives.

My billing and benefits experience is direct. As a Billing Specialist at PCMH (2012–2014), I handled client billing, payments, and collections, monitored accounts receivable, assisted clients with payment plans, and created reports for the CEO and COO. I have helped clients understand their bills, including explaining explanations of benefits, in plain language and without rushing them. As a Human Resource Manager with Milan Health Care Center and Reliant Care Management Company, I was trusted with resident trust funds, made daily bank deposits, completed daily and monthly reconciliation, and served as an accounts receivable specialist. I would bring that same accuracy and discretion to intake paperwork, financial conversations with families, and admissions records, where a mistake or a confusing explanation adds stress a family does not need.

Working with people in a care setting runs through all of that work. In long-term care I assisted residents and families directly, served as safety manager, monitored OSHA compliance and compliance with corporate and state regulations and training, and conducted bi-weekly all-staff meetings. In those roles I also served as a CPR Instructor and a CALM Instructor, training staff as part of my duties — experience that taught me to stay calm, listen first, and communicate clearly when people are upset or afraid. In medical customer service at Hometown Medical, I helped patients directly with their questions and concerns. I aim to bring that same empathetic, caring approach to adolescents and their families during admission, while handling each step promptly and efficiently.

Admissions also depends on steady coordination, and management has been a constant in my career. As Property Manager for Centerville Rentals, I oversaw 90 units, conducted inspections, issued work orders, and supervised maintenance. As Store Manager at 7th Heaven, I supervised employees and handled interviews, orientation, and training. Across those roles I have kept schedules, files, and follow-up organized, and communicated between families, staff, and leadership so nothing fell through the cracks — the same follow-through needed to move an admission from first call to first day.

I am proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint) and very familiar with QuickBooks, and I have worked in numerous other business and billing programs. My Columbia College (Online) coursework in 2010–2011, where I completed all core business administration classes, including financial and managerial accounting and economics, supports that experience.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could serve your program and the families who turn to it. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,
Christina Worley

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a bachelor's degree in Psychology and as a graduate student pursuing a master's in Counseling and Art Therapy, I have developed a strong foundation in mental health, substance use treatment, and providing compassionate support to individuals during challenging times.

My professional experience includes working in a behavioral health hospital, including the detox setting, where I gained valuable experience supporting individuals navigating substance use and mental health challenges. Additionally, in my current clinical internship at the Mary Jo Rolli Codey Center, I have had the opportunity to complete client intakes, engage with individuals and families, and gain experience with the initial stages of the therapeutic process. These experiences have strengthened my ability to communicate sensitively, build rapport, gather important client information, and approach each individual with empathy and professionalism.

My current experience as a Crisis Counselor in a behavioral school setting has further developed my interpersonal and communication skills, as well as my ability to navigate challenging situations while maintaining a supportive and client-centered approach.
