Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. With a professional background in healthcare administration, patient coordination, educational administration, and human resources, I am confident in my ability to provide compassionate and efficient support to adolescents and families seeking treatment.

In my current role as a Medical Secretary at Premier Medical Group, I serve as a point of contact for patients navigating their healthcare needs. My responsibilities include managing high-volume telephone communications, coordinating appointments and referrals, maintaining confidential patient records, and communicating with physicians and clinical staff. This experience has strengthened my ability to handle sensitive conversations with empathy, discretion, and professionalism.

My previous experience within the Poughkeepsie City School District has also given me an appreciation for the importance of supporting young people and their families. Combined with my human resources background, I have developed strong interpersonal, organizational, and problem-solving skills that would translate effectively into an admissions-focused environment.

I am particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s commitment to supporting adolescents experiencing mental health and substance use challenges. I understand that reaching out for treatment can be an overwhelming and emotional experience for families, and I would welcome the opportunity to help make that initial step more comfortable, supportive, and accessible.

I am eager to bring my healthcare experience, compassion, and dedication to your team while expanding my knowledge of behavioral health admissions.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications can contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,

Jacqulin Jetter

candidates.cover_letter:
I am writing to express my strong interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a background combining direct healthcare support, remote customer service, and operations management—alongside fluency in both English and Spanish—I am confident in my ability to guide families through the admissions process with empathy, clarity, and efficiency.  
In my previous role as a Patient Care Technician at Jefferson Einstein, I worked directly with patients and their loved ones during sensitive and high-stress moments. That experience taught me how to listen actively, de-escalate concerns, and maintain composure while coordinating critical care details. Pairing this clinical empathy with my experience handling high-volume remote inquiries at Conduent allows me to connect meaningfully with parents and adolescents over the phone and via virtual channels, ensuring they feel supported from their very first point of contact.
Additionally, my supervisory background at Quail Ridge and Sunrise of Metairie required meticulous organization, family communication, and seamless coordination across multidisciplinary teams. Whether managing intake workflows, verifying essential documentation, or following up with prospective families, I thrive in structured, fast-paced environments where accuracy and compassion go hand in hand. Being bilingual in English and Spanish also enables me to bridge communication gaps and ensure a wider range of families receive clear, accessible guidance when seeking treatment options.
Currently completing my Bachelor of Business Administration in Human Resource Management at Western Governors University, I bring a strong foundation in ethical communication, confidentiality, and people-centered operations. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my healthcare background, remote communication skills, and dedication to supporting families can contribute to the admissions team at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Ja’Han Williams-Holloway

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With my background in crisis intervention, behavioral health screenings, customer service, and remote operations, I believe my experience aligns well with the responsibilities of this position.

In my current role as a 211/988 Crisis Specialist with Heart of Florida United Way, I assist individuals and families experiencing mental health challenges, emotional distress, substance use concerns, and other difficult circumstances. My responsibilities include conducting screenings, gathering confidential information, assessing individual needs, documenting interactions accurately, and connecting callers with appropriate resources and services. This experience has strengthened my ability to approach sensitive conversations with compassion, patience, and professionalism.

My previous professional experience has also allowed me to develop strong skills in data entry, navigating multiple systems, maintaining confidential records, and managing responsibilities independently in a remote environment. Additionally, I have experience developing training materials, updating procedures, and assisting new employees.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to continue supporting individuals and families while becoming more involved in the admissions process and helping them access ongoing treatment. I recognize how overwhelming seeking mental health or substance use treatment can be, and I value the opportunity to make that process more approachable and supportive.

I am confident that my combination of crisis intervention experience, attention to detail, communication skills, and commitment to helping others would make me a valuable addition to your team. I am also eager to expand my knowledge of insurance verification, admissions coordination, and electronic medical record systems.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and skills can contribute to your programs.

Sincerely,
Sarai

I am writing to express my interest in the Mental Health Support position with your organization. While my professional background has primarily been in cosmetology, my passion for supporting others has been shaped by both my work experience and my personal life.

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With more than 10 years of experience in administrative operations, student and employee support, behavior intervention, and human resources, I believe I bring a valuable combination of interpersonal, organizational, and problem-solving skills that would translate well into this position.

One of the most meaningful parts of my professional background comes from my six years at Loring Job Corps Center, where I worked in a federally funded educational and career-training environment serving students between the ages of 16 and 24. Much of my work involved behavior intervention and supporting young adults who were navigating difficult personal circumstances, behavioral challenges, and barriers to achieving their goals. I worked directly with students and their families, developed and implemented individualized performance improvement plans, addressed behavioral concerns, conducted investigations, and helped students recognize their potential while encouraging accountability and positive change.

That experience taught me the importance of meeting people where they are, listening without judgment, communicating expectations clearly, and recognizing that the circumstances behind someone’s behavior are not always immediately visible. I understand that reaching out for mental health or substance use treatment can be an incredibly difficult first step, not only for the individual but also for their family. I would bring that understanding to every interaction, recognizing that the initial conversation can have a meaningful impact on someone’s willingness to pursue help.

My professional experience also includes remote human resources operations, healthcare administration, onboarding, confidential records management, compliance, and coordinating processes across multiple departments. At Phaidon International, I worked remotely while managing high-volume onboarding and orientation responsibilities for employees nationwide. This required independent time management, consistent follow-up, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities without relying on daily supervision. My experience in healthcare administration also provided exposure to insurance-related coordination and the importance of accuracy when handling sensitive information.

In addition to my professional background, I am currently pursuing my Bachelor of Arts in Psychology through the University of Maine. My education has further strengthened my interest in human behavior, mental health, and the factors that influence individual well-being. I see this opportunity as a meaningful way to bring together my professional experience and academic pursuits while continuing to develop within the behavioral health field.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to the operational goals of both Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center while helping individuals and families navigate the admissions process with compassion, clarity, and professionalism. I am particularly interested in joining an organization where I can continue learning, take on new responsibilities, and grow professionally while contributing to work that makes a meaningful difference in people’s lives.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Kayla Pike

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

Sometimes the most important part of someone’s journey toward healing is the first person who answers the phone. That interaction can shape whether a family feels overwhelmed or reassured, uncertain or hopeful, and whether taking that next step toward help feels a little less intimidating. My heart is to bring compassion and care into those interactions, which is what makes the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy particularly meaningful to me.

I hold a bachelor’s degree in Psychology and bring over three years of experience supporting a nonprofit organization across five centers. In my current role, I coordinate scheduling and operations across multiple locations, working with different systems and teams to ensure that services run smoothly and individuals receive the support they need.

One aspect of my work that I am particularly passionate about is improving the client experience. I have worked alongside women and families navigating crisis, many facing significant financial, emotional, and personal challenges. Recognizing the need for more accessible support, I took the initiative to develop a client resource website that brings referrals, community resources, and additional support together in one place. I believe in looking beyond the immediate task, identifying where people need additional support, and finding practical ways to make a difference.

I would bring that same initiative and compassion to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I understand that seeking mental health or substance use treatment for an adolescent can be an incredibly vulnerable step for a family. I would approach each interaction with patience, sensitivity, and genuine care, while ensuring the admissions process remains organized and efficient.

With my psychology background, coordination experience, bilingual communication skills in English and Spanish, and commitment to meaningful service, I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your team.

Thank you for your consideration. I look forward to the possibility of discussing how I could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Warm regards,
Raquel

work_history.summary: Responsible for maintaining security, order, and safety within the facility by supervising inmate activities, conducting searches for contraband, documenting behavioral observations and incidents, and ensuring accountability of tools, equipment, and facility keys. Duties include responding to medical emergencies, addressing disruptive or abnormal behavior, administering appropriate disciplinary actions or physical restraints when necessary, and managing inmate movements both within the facility and during transport, while consistently upholding policies, procedures, and safety protocols.

work_history.title: Flight Operations Flight Crew
work_history.summary: This position serves as an in-flight attendant responsible for the safety and security of the passengers on board. The primary responsibilities of this position are to meticulously execute pre-flight safety checks in adherence to Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) regulations, and demonstration of safety and emergency measures on board to customers to include functioning as a first responder in flight in the event of any medical, safety or security emergency. This position is safety and security focused and requires extensive training on safety and security procedures as well as federal regulations to include reporting requirements as dictated by company policy and federal law.

work_history.title: Judicial Marshal State Law Enforcement Officer
work_history.summary: This position serves as a state law enforcement officer under chapter 78 section 6 of the Connecticut General Assembly. The primary responsibilities of this role are to ensure the integrity of the judicial process by maintaining the security and safety of the courthouse staff, visitors and inmates as well as the physical facility. This equates to executing training, tactics and procedures to facilitate secure judicial proceedings, transport and secure inmates, deter, detect and suppress acts of violence and mischief and ensure safe and secure operations 24 hours a day. This position directly interacts with inmates and detainees awaiting trial within the Connecticut judicial system. This includes ensuring the safe and secure transport of inmates and detainees between holding and correctional facilities and the in-processing of this population into a secured facility. Furthermore, this position is tasked with access control of a secured courthouse facility, executing orders to remand subjects to custody and responding to emergencies within the facility and its outlying properties. This necessitates the position to execute overt patrols of the interior and exterior of the structure, facilitate internal prisoner movements and limit access to secured areas. Moreover, this position was tasked to supervise access control points and screen entrants for proper identification, contraband and demeanor. This includes denying entry to those who do not meet the proper criteria, detaining subjects as required and using all necessary force to compel compliance. In addition, this position is required to be competent with access control systems such as logical access badges, closed circuit televisions, electronic monitoring devices and various other physical security devices. This position required completion of a rigorous 4-month training academy with the State of Connecticut including a physical techniques and tactics training regiment, defensive driving course and basic law enforcement practices consistent with that of a traditional police academy. These principles include use of force, searches and seizures, evidentiary procedures/ chain of custody and authority and jurisdiction.

candidates.cover_letter:
To Whom It May Concern,
	I am a New Orleans resident. I have four children ages 10-15 years old. In my personal and professional life I have utilized my educational background in human development to support communities and individuals during periods of trial and transition. 
	I feel compassionately compelled to support individuals in crisis. I did so professionally for the first time at a women’s shelter in Virginia called Project Horizon. I worked the overnight shift answering inbound calls on the sexual assault and suicide hotline, receiving new intakes, providing access to resources and explaining policies and proceedures. I assessed callers for which services they would be fit for and matched them with resources in their area. I explained over the phone in simple, calm, caring language that they made a good choice in reaching out to connect to me and start the journey to a safer, healthier life. In this role I served as a literal lifeline on many occasions, and I am proud to have been a small part of keeping each person alive and fighting. 
	In my work as a Family Support Coordinator I managed therapeutic teams and acted as a liaison for families to ensure that the clients' needs were met. In that work I confirmed healthcare insurance status, and kept files up to date. I regularly followed with families and fulfilled all state mandated requirements, keeping track of every contact in dated records. I kept all HIPPA requirements of privacy in all aspects of my work. As a Family Support Coordinator I 80% of my time was spent in a work-from-home environment. I managed my own time, fulfilled my caseload requirements, and communicated regularly with my professional teammates. I found a work-from-home environment allowed me to focus my attention without interruption from officemates or the requirements of coordinating the use of office equipment. I confidently conducted necessary conversations over the phone or via email in a warm, but professional tone. I found that I preferred working from home as a more effective professional model.
	I have been volunteering with my local adolescent community for more about 17 years. My compassion and concern for  the physical and emotional health of teens has grown over that time. As a parent of teenagers myself, I have become even more acutely aware of the stresses and pressures that teens face day-to-day. I find that teens usually only want to accept help, from the right person, at the right time, with the right resources. As Virtual Admissions Coordinator: Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment I believe with my background and experiences I can be an asset to teens needing access to support on their journey to sobriety and a healthy mental state. Thank you for your time and consideration of my application.

Sincerely,
Sarah Ortiz

In my current role as a 988 Crisis Counselor at Crisis Center, Inc., and previously as a CARES Crisis Line Supervisor at Chrysalis (a fully remote position), I have supported youth and adults in acute emotional and behavioral distress via phone, text, and chat. At Chrysalis, I partnered directly with parents, hospitals, school personnel, and local SASS agencies to develop crisis safety plans, verify Medicaid/HMO coverage, and connect families with community-based mental health resources while maintaining strict HIPAA compliance. Working remotely also honed my ability to navigate multiple digital portals simultaneously, maintain rapid and accurate Electronic Health Record (EHR) documentation, and coach team members to deliver consistent, compassionate care.

Beyond crisis response, my hands-on work as a Certified Behavioral Health Technician (BHT) at Midwest Center for Youth and Families and a Youth Care Worker at Crisis Center grounded me in adolescent development, DBT skills, trauma-informed de-escalation, and individualized service plan implementation. Whether collaborating with families to navigate care barriers or mentoring teens through daily behavioral goals, I am deeply committed to helping young people feel heard, supported, and empowered in their wellness journey.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my remote crisis-support expertise, youth behavioral health background, and dedication to family-centered care to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for your time and consideration, and I look forward to discussing how I can contribute to your team.

Sincerely,  
Caijone Jones

Sincerely, 
Ashley Mayo

Dear Hiring Manager,
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. Throughout my career in admissions, recruiting, human resources, and client services, I have been driven by one core goal: helping people navigate important life decisions with compassion, professionalism, and support. The opportunity to serve individuals and families seeking mental health and substance use treatment is meaningful work that aligns strongly with my strengths and values.
In my current role as an Admissions Representative, I serve as the first point of contact for prospective students who are exploring educational opportunities and major life changes. Through phone calls, virtual meetings, text messages, and email communication, I guide individuals through the admissions process, answer questions, address concerns, coordinate next steps, and ensure each person feels heard and supported. I understand that many people reach out during stressful or uncertain times, and I take pride in creating a welcoming and reassuring experience from the very first interaction.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am writing to express my interest in the Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a professional background in behavioral health, substance use treatment, admissions, and case management, I am passionate about helping individuals and families navigate the often overwhelming process of accessing quality mental health care.

In my previous role as an Admissions Coordinator at Fairland Recovery Center, I managed the admissions process from initial inquiry through admission. My responsibilities included conducting patient prescreenings, coordinating insurance verification, reviewing clinical information, facilitating appropriate placement, maintaining accurate patient records, and collaborating with clinical teams, business development representatives, and referral sources. I developed a strong ability to build rapport quickly, navigate sensitive conversations with compassion, overcome barriers to treatment, and manage multiple prospective admissions simultaneously.

I hold an Associate of Applied Science in Social Work and am currently a senior pursuing my bachelor’s degree in Social Work. My professional credentials include CARES, CPS-AD, CADC-T, Trauma-Informed Care training, and certifications as an Addictions Specialist and Domestic and Family Violence Specialist.

Throughout my career, I have served in various behavioral health roles, including case management, housing coordination, group facilitation, counseling, and patient advocacy. These experiences have provided me with a comprehensive understanding of the treatment process and the importance of effective communication, confidentiality, empathy, and continuity of care.

I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to work with adolescents and their families because I believe early intervention, compassionate support, and access to appropriate treatment can profoundly impact the trajectory of a young person’s life. I understand that admissions is more than an administrative process—it is often a family’s first point of contact during one of the most vulnerable moments of their lives. I take that responsibility seriously.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my admissions experience, clinical knowledge, organizational skills, and genuine passion for helping others to Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am confident that my ability to balance compassionate patient care with operational efficiency would make me a valuable addition to your team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications align with your organization’s needs.

Sincerely,

Alexandria Towery

Dear Hiring Team,

Thank you for reaching out about the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. While I have not held a behavioral health admissions role or a fully remote position, my background has prepared me well for both.

I spent five years as a Registered Behavior Technician, working with children and their families in clinics, homes, and the community. Before that, I was a caseworker at Parkland Hospital, where I conducted intake interviews and health assessments, referred clients to resources, and kept confidential records. Those jobs taught me how to listen and communicate clearly with families in difficult situations. It also taught me how to be the calm and stabilizing force when things seem complicated or uncertain. Making a positive impact on clients and their families was deeply fulfilling, and I would like to continue that kind of work.

In my current leasing role, I follow up on every lead in a CRM and guide people from first inquiry through screening, approval, and move-in. At Aurum Apartments, I managed my own pipeline, deadlines, and duties, and I am used to working independently and holding myself accountable without daily direction. Every job I have held, from retail to healthcare to leasing, has been client-focused, so serving people well is the one thing I have always done. My coursework in couples and family therapy also helps me communicate with parents and teens when they are struggling. This combined experience allows me to bring empathy and compassion to my daily interactions serving others.

I am confident in my ability to stay calm, pay attention to details, and follow through, while showing care and compassion. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Christina

Application for: Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Adolescent Wellness Academy

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a bachelor’s degree in Psychology and four years of professional experience in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), I believe I bring a valuable combination of behavioral health knowledge, interpersonal communication skills, and experience supporting children, adolescents, and their families.

Throughout my career as a Registered Behavior Technician, I have worked closely with individuals with varying developmental and behavioral needs. My responsibilities have required me to establish trust with clients and caregivers, communicate effectively with families, collaborate with clinical professionals, document progress, and navigate challenging situations with patience and professionalism.

One of the most important things my experience has taught me is that working in behavioral health requires more than understanding behavior. It requires recognizing that every individual and family has unique circumstances, challenges, and needs. Building rapport, listening without judgment, and helping families feel supported are essential parts of providing meaningful care.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it would allow me to apply my background in psychology and behavioral health in a different capacity. I understand that contacting a mental health treatment provider can be an overwhelming experience for families. I would take seriously the responsibility of being one of their first points of contact and helping them navigate the next steps toward appropriate treatment.

Although my professional background has primarily been in direct behavioral services rather than formal admissions coordination, I have developed transferable skills in family communication, clinical documentation, professional collaboration, and individualized support. I am comfortable learning new systems and procedures and would be eager to develop additional experience with admissions workflows, insurance verification, and electronic medical record platforms.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, work ethic, and genuine interest in behavioral health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of discussing how my background could contribute to your team.

Professional Background

Relevant Professional Experience

Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) / Applied Behavior Analysis

* Demonstrated the ability to establish trust with families while maintaining appropriate professional boundaries.

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am a certified clinical medical assistant, and I spent almost two years as the only medical assistant in a busy specialty practice, where most of my day was spent talking with patients and families on the phone and through the patient portal.

In that role I handled intake calls, gathered patient information, verified insurance, scheduled appointments, and helped people through stressful and sometimes embarrassing situations with patience and privacy. Patients and families are often at their most anxious on that first call, and I learned how much it helps when the person on the other end is calm, clear, and kind. I also hold an associate degree in business, which has helped me stay organized while juggling a high volume of calls, messages, and documentation in the electronic health record.

The admissions side of care matters to me because it is where treatment actually begins. When a family reaches out for help for their teenager, that first conversation can decide whether they follow through. I would love the chance to be that steady first voice for the families you serve.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the chance to speak with you about the role.
Sincerely,
Sydney Heaton

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting your adolescent mental health and substance use treatment programs. What immediately drew me to this opportunity is the importance of being the first person someone encounters when they are reaching out for help. I would value the opportunity to bring my communication, coordination, administrative, and people-management experience to a role where those skills can make a meaningful difference.

Throughout my career, I have worked in positions requiring strong communication, organization, discretion, and the ability to remain composed when dealing with challenging situations. As the owner and operator of a remodeling business, I was responsible for managing customers, employees, subcontractors, schedules, finances, payroll, HR administration, and competing priorities simultaneously. I learned how important it is to listen carefully, ask the right questions, communicate clearly, and follow through on what people need.

My experience has also given me a strong administrative foundation. I have handled detailed documentation, data entry, electronic records, invoicing, payroll, HR administration, and customer communication. In my most recent industrial role, I worked with Procore and Excel to maintain project documentation and reviewed paperwork for accuracy and organization.

I am also currently pursuing undergraduate studies in Forensic Psychology and Business Management.  I am especially interested in opportunities where I can combine my professional experience with my growing understanding of people, communication, and human behavior.

I understand that someone contacting a treatment program may be reaching out during an extremely difficult moment. I would approach every interaction with patience, compassion, professionalism, and respect while helping the individual or family understand the next steps available to them. I am comfortable learning new systems and procedures, handling sensitive information appropriately, and coordinating details to ensure that people do not feel lost in the process.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my work ethic, life experience, organizational strengths, and genuine desire to help people to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss how my background could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Shauna Ballard

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I have a deep appreciation for the importance of accessible mental health care, and the opportunity to help individuals and families navigate their first steps toward treatment is one I would approach with genuine compassion, patience, and dedication.

Throughout my professional experience in customer service and other fast-paced environments, I’ve developed strong communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills. I’ve learned how important it is to listen attentively, remain composed during difficult conversations, and ensure that every person I interact with receives the attention and respect they deserve. I believe these qualities are especially valuable when working with individuals who may be experiencing some of the most vulnerable moments of their lives.

Mental health advocacy is deeply important to me, and I recognize how intimidating and overwhelming seeking treatment can be, particularly for adolescents, families, and individuals struggling with substance use. I want to help make that process more approachable by offering reassurance, clear communication, and dependable guidance from the very first interaction.

I am detail-oriented, adaptable, and committed to learning new systems and procedures. I understand the importance of confidentiality, accurate documentation, consistent follow-through, and treating every inquiry with professionalism and empathy.

What appeals to me most about this opportunity is the ability to contribute to meaningful work. I would be proud to support an organization dedicated to helping people access the care they need and ensuring that every person who reaches out is treated with dignity.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, dedication, and interpersonal skills could contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Kyle Felizardo

November 24, 2026

Hiring Committee
Adolescent Wellness Academy & Principles Recovery Center

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. As a recent graduate of Grand Canyon University with a bachelor's degree in Behavioral Health Science and professional experience working with adolescents, families, and educators, I am eager to contribute to an organization dedicated to helping individuals access meaningful mental health and substance use treatment.

In my current role as a Library-Media Coordinator at Marina Village Middle School, I work directly with adolescents from diverse backgrounds, including students with emotional, behavioral, and developmental challenges. My position requires patience, empathy, active listening, and the ability to adapt my communication to individual needs. I independently manage daily operations, respond to inquiries, maintain accurate records, coordinate programs, and balance competing priorities with minimal supervision.

My academic background has provided me with a strong foundation in mental health, substance use disorders, ethical practices, cultural sensitivity, and evidence-based interventions. For my undergraduate capstone, I developed a comprehensive proposal for an inclusive summer program supporting children with emotional and behavioral health challenges. This project strengthened my understanding of the barriers families face when seeking appropriate services and the importance of connecting individuals with resources that meet their unique needs.

Additionally, my experience as an independent consultant with Rodan + Fields has strengthened my customer service, remote communication, outreach, and follow-up skills. I understand the importance of asking thoughtful questions, establishing trust, maintaining consistent communication, and guiding individuals toward informed decisions.

While my professional background has not followed a traditional behavioral health admissions pathway, I bring relevant education, experience supporting adolescents, strong organizational skills, and a genuine commitment to helping others. I am eager to develop proficiency in your admissions procedures, insurance verification processes, and CRM and EMR systems while maintaining the highest standards of confidentiality and professionalism.

I recognize that reaching out for behavioral health treatment can be an overwhelming and vulnerable experience for individuals and their families. I would welcome the opportunity to be a compassionate and dependable first point of contact, helping callers feel heard, supported, and confident in taking their next steps toward treatment.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my education, professional experience, and dedication to behavioral health can contribute to your admissions team.

Sincerely,

Kimberly Valdez

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. I am currently pursuing my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling at Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center and hold a bachelor’s degree in Psychology from Texas Tech University. I am passionate about increasing access to mental health services and helping individuals and families navigate the process of seeking treatment.

Through my clinical practicum at Elevate Counseling Group, I have gained direct experience responding to prospective client inquiries, conducting client intakes and biopsychosocial assessments, evaluating presenting concerns, building therapeutic rapport, and maintaining confidential clinical documentation. These experiences have strengthened my ability to navigate sensitive conversations with empathy, gather relevant clinical information, and establish trust with individuals seeking mental health services. I have a particular interest in working with adolescents and young adults and recognize the importance of early intervention and family involvement in treatment.

In addition to my clinical experience, I bring a strong professional background in remote operations and administration. My current role requires me to independently manage competing priorities, coordinate complex processes, maintain accurate records, and communicate effectively with a diverse range of individuals. I am highly organized, adaptable, technologically proficient, and comfortable working independently in a fast-paced virtual environment.

What draws me to this position is the opportunity to combine my clinical training and administrative experience in a meaningful way. I understand that seeking mental health or substance use treatment can be an overwhelming and vulnerable experience for both individuals and their families. I believe the admissions process plays an essential role in establishing trust, reducing barriers to treatment, and helping families feel supported and informed as they navigate their options.

As a future Licensed Professional Counselor, I am deeply committed to improving access to quality mental health care. I believe my combination of hands-on clinical intake experience, educational background, professional communication skills, and administrative expertise would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to your admissions team.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

What caught my attention about your admissions position was the opportunity to be a reassuring first point of contact for someone who may not know where to turn. I would like to help individuals and families seeking mental health or substance use treatment feel heard and understand their next steps.

While living in Gibraltar, I facilitated a Down syndrome support group for families. That experience reinforced the importance of listening without judgment and giving people room to share their concerns. In my current preschool enrichment role, I work with children in the City of San Antonio’s federally funded Head Start program. One of the most rewarding parts of my work is earning the trust of children who are initially fearful or reluctant to participate. Patience and consistency make a difference.

My background as a longtime yoga instructor and studio owner has also given me experience answering client questions, coordinating schedules and adapting my communication to individual needs. I served military families in a federal fitness position with U.S. Navy Morale, Welfare and Recreation in Naples, Italy. As a former military spouse, I understand how challenging it can be for families to find their footing in unfamiliar circumstances.

In my recent remote contract work, I reviewed AI-assisted conversations and stepped in when human judgment was needed, communicating through digital messaging and live video. My retail management and independent business experience have taught me to take responsibility for concerns, stay organized and recognize when additional assistance is necessary.

I earned my Associate of Arts degree in 2024. My background is in nonclinical wellness and family support rather than formal behavioral health admissions. I am eager to learn your intake procedures, treatment programs, insurance verification and confidential documentation systems. I would appreciate the opportunity to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. Thank you for considering my application.

Sincerely,

J. Noelle Hoth

Dear Hiring Team,

I'm applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. When someone calls a treatment program, they are often scared and unsure of what to do next. I want to be the person who answers with warmth and gets them to a clear next step.

At the American Red Cross, I coordinate intake appointments, answer incoming calls, register clients, and follow up. I also keep confidential client profiles and send weekly reports to regional leadership.

Thank you for your time. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can support your admissions team and the families who call you.

Sincerely,
Anthony Martinez

I understand firsthand the fear, uncertainty, and emotional exhaustion that families can experience when trying to find appropriate treatment. My family has navigated hospitalizations, mental health crises, and community-based behavioral health services, including the YES Waiver program. Through those experiences, I witnessed how compassionate professionals can make an extraordinary difference in the lives of both adolescents and their families.

Those experiences strengthened my desire to pursue a career in mental health advocacy. They also taught me the importance of listening without judgment, communicating with empathy, and helping families feel supported during some of their most vulnerable moments. I recognize that an admissions coordinator may be one of the first people a struggling adolescent or concerned parent speaks with, and I would approach that responsibility with professionalism, patience, compassion, and respect.

I am particularly interested in the opportunity to assist families throughout the admissions process, coordinate necessary information, communicate with treatment teams, and help individuals better understand their options for care. My background in telephone-based customer service, healthcare documentation, insurance-related inquiries, and administrative support would allow me to contribute meaningfully while continuing to develop my knowledge of adolescent mental health and substance use treatment.

As I pursue my long-term goal of earning a Master of Social Work, I am seeking an opportunity where my professional skills and personal passion can come together to make a meaningful difference. I would be honored to contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s work supporting adolescents and helping families find hope, guidance, and access to appropriate treatment.

matters to me. When a parent calls about mental health or substance use treatment for their teen, they

families know what happens next.

forensic psychology and my training as a Christian Mental Health Coach have deepened my interest in

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to talk with you about how I can support your admissions team and the families who reach out to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,
Lizmar Encarnacion-Rosario

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a bachelor's degree in Psychology, ongoing graduate studies in Social Work, and professional experience in behavioral health intake, case management, and substance use support, I bring a combination of clinical understanding, administrative coordination, and compassionate communication. As a bilingual English- and Spanish-speaking professional, I am especially passionate about helping individuals and families overcome barriers to accessing mental health and substance use treatment.

In my current role as a Case Manager at EMC Behavioral, I work in a fully virtual environment, supporting children and adolescents experiencing mental health and substance use challenges. My responsibilities include conducting intake assessments, identifying service needs, verifying insurance, coordinating referrals, scheduling appointments, and maintaining accurate client documentation. Working remotely has strengthened my ability to independently manage my responsibilities, communicate effectively with clients and caregivers through virtual platforms, and ensure timely follow-up without requiring daily in-person supervision. I understand the importance of maintaining confidentiality, accurate documentation, and consistent communication when coordinating behavioral health services remotely.

Additionally, as a Bilingual Parent Support Specialist at Catholic Charities' Guadalupe Home, I support young mothers experiencing various challenges, including substance use concerns, in a residential shelter environment. My work involves providing trauma-informed support, assisting with behavioral and emotional challenges, communicating with residents, and maintaining accurate documentation. Working with individuals during vulnerable periods has taught me the importance of approaching difficult conversations with empathy, patience, and professionalism while helping individuals feel respected and supported.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because both programs serve populations with whom I have direct professional experience. I understand that individuals and families seeking behavioral health or substance use treatment may feel overwhelmed, uncertain, or afraid. I believe that providing clear information, listening without judgment, and following through on next steps can make a meaningful difference in their willingness and ability to access care. My experience with insurance verification, intake coordination, appointment scheduling, and client communication, combined with my ability to work independently in a fully remote environment, aligns closely with the responsibilities of this position.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my behavioral health experience, organizational skills, and bilingual communication abilities to your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background can support your programs and the individuals and families you serve.

Sincerely,
Jennyfer Alvidrez

I am drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy because of your commitment to connection, compassion, and individualized care. candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in Adolescent Mental Health and Substance Use Treatment. With over 10 years of experience in healthcare and senior care, along with a strong background in patient coordination, admissions, scheduling, insurance authorizations, and customer service, I believe I can make a valuable contribution to your team.

Throughout my career, I have developed strong communication and organizational skills while working closely with patients, families, healthcare providers, and insurance companies. My experience includes coordinating patient admissions, managing referrals, verifying insurance authorizations, handling sensitive information, answering inquiries, and ensuring that individuals receive timely assistance and appropriate support.

I hold certifications as a Certified Nursing Assistant, Medical Assistant, and Psychiatric Technician. These qualifications, combined with my hands-on healthcare experience, have given me a strong understanding of patient needs, confidentiality, compassionate communication, and the importance of treating every individual with dignity and respect.

I am particularly interested in this opportunity because I value helping individuals and families navigate challenging situations and access the care they need. I understand that families seeking adolescent mental health or substance use treatment may be experiencing uncertainty, stress, and emotional challenges. I would bring patience, empathy, professionalism, and a nonjudgmental approach to every interaction.

Additionally, I am bilingual in English and Spanish, comfortable with technology and electronic documentation systems, and experienced in coordinating multiple responsibilities in fast-paced healthcare environments. I am confident in my ability to manage virtual admissions inquiries, communicate effectively with families, coordinate with clinical teams, and help facilitate a smooth admissions process.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my healthcare background, administrative experience, and commitment to compassionate patient care could benefit your organization.

Sincerely,
Maria Gabriela Morales

November 24, 2026

Adolescent Wellness Academy Talent Acquisition Team

RE: Program Director – Virtual IOP | Adolescent Behavioral Health

Dear Hiring Committee:

Adolescent Wellness Academy’s virtual IOP requires a leader who can balance clinical quality with the operational discipline to grow access, sustain census and build trusted referral relationships. My experience spans behavioral health program startup, executive healthcare operations, telehealth service delivery and national child and family services, positioning me to help expand a high-quality virtual program for adolescents and their families.

As Director of Residential Treatment Facilities at Concept Health Systems, I launched a newly licensed behavioral health program and built the staffing, policies, partnerships and workflows required for sustainable operations. I directed multidisciplinary services, budgeting, licensing, accreditation and workforce development, independently securing partnerships for medication-assisted treatment, pharmacy services and integrated medical care. The program maintained 100% occupancy for 33 of 36 months, including throughout the pandemic.

At Optum, I delivered behavioral health services in a large-scale telehealth environment, applying evidence-based approaches to engagement and care coordination. I ranked among the top-performing providers based on performance analytics, participant satisfaction and program success measures. That direct virtual-care experience informs how I would support clinical teams, monitor engagement and strengthen the participant experience in a virtual IOP.

At Urban Strategies, as Assistant Program Director and Interim Director, I helped scale an ORR child and family services program nationwide, developing standardized processes, specialty-service structures and quality controls. My earlier school assessment, truancy court and child advocacy work also provides a practical understanding of the systems surrounding adolescents and their caregivers.

I would bring AWA a growth-oriented approach to school and provider outreach, referral conversion, census forecasting, staffing coverage, audit readiness and leadership reporting, working closely with licensed clinical leaders on treatment quality. Based in Tampa, I welcome the opportunity to help build a sustainable virtual IOP that expands access to timely, family-centered behavioral healthcare across Florida.

Sincerely,
Chantel George, M.Ed.

Re: Program Director, Virtual IOP | Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Committee,

I am writing to express my interest in the Program Director position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Barry University, a Bachelor of Science in Psychology from Florida A&M University, and professional experience spanning behavioral health quality assurance, team supervision, program leadership, and psychological research, I bring a multidisciplinary perspective to clinical program development and leadership.

My professional background has allowed me to develop an understanding of behavioral health services from both clinical and operational perspectives. In my current capacity as a Mental Health Quality Assurance Specialist and Supervisor, I oversee a team while supporting clinical quality, documentation standards, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement. This experience has strengthened my ability to evaluate clinical processes, support staff accountability, identify opportunities for improvement, and maintain standards that promote safe, ethical, and effective care. I understand that successful behavioral health programming requires more than quality clinical services; it requires intentional leadership, operational consistency, and a commitment to measurable outcomes.

Additionally, my leadership experience in a museum setting has strengthened my ability to coordinate people, support organizational objectives, and engage with diverse communities. These experiences, combined with my behavioral health background, have shaped my approach to leadership as one grounded in collaboration, communication, accountability, and relationship-building.

My academic and research experiences have further informed my commitment to culturally responsive and family-centered mental health services. Through my graduate training and international research experience in Bali, Indonesia, I explored the intersections of cultural identity, spirituality, resilience, social support, and psychological well-being. These experiences reinforced the importance of understanding individuals within their broader family, cultural, and social environments. I am particularly interested in ensuring that adolescents and their families have access to mental health services that recognize their individual needs while addressing the systems and circumstances that influence their well-being.

I am especially drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy’s family-centered approach and its commitment to providing structured behavioral health services to adolescents. The opportunity to contribute to the growth of a virtual Intensive Outpatient Program is exciting because it brings together several areas of my professional interests: clinical quality, program leadership, community engagement, team development, and accessible mental health care.

I would welcome the opportunity to contribute my clinical knowledge, supervisory experience, research perspective, and commitment to organizational excellence to AWA. I am confident that my interdisciplinary background would allow me to bring a thoughtful, collaborative, and quality-driven approach to the continued development of your Virtual IOP.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and professional goals align with Adolescent Wellness Academy’s mission.

Sincerely,

Gabriela C. Sevrin, M.S.

Dear AWA Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Program Director, Virtual IOP – Adolescent Behavioral Health position. I have worked with a few of you closely already! As a licensed therapist with over 10 years of experience in behavioral healthcare, including serving as Director of Admissions at Galen Hope, I bring a unique combination of clinical expertise, operational leadership, and a genuine passion for improving access to quality mental health treatment.

Throughout my career, I have worked extensively with adolescents and families navigating complex mental health challenges, including anxiety, depression, eating disorders, and co-occurring conditions. As a licensed clinician, I understand the importance of evidence-based treatment, family involvement, and individualized care, particularly during the critical developmental years of adolescence.

In my previous leadership role, I oversaw admissions operations, led and trained teams, streamlined workflows, monitored performance metrics, and collaborated closely with clinical, administrative, and business development departments. My experience navigating levels of care, including PHP and IOP, has given me a strong understanding of the clinical and operational considerations necessary to deliver effective treatment while maintaining high standards of patient care.

What particularly excites me about this opportunity is the ability to combine my clinical background with my strengths in leadership, program development, and operational strategy. I understand that a successful virtual IOP requires more than strong clinical programming; it requires an engaged team, efficient systems, meaningful family collaboration, and an environment where adolescents feel supported and connected, even through a screen.

I pride myself on being an approachable, collaborative, and solutions-oriented leader who values both clinical excellence and the people responsible for delivering it. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, energy, and commitment to adolescent mental health to AWA, helping strengthen and grow a program that makes meaningful treatment accessible to more families.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and leadership approach align with AWA's mission.

Warm regards,

Chloe Godward

candidates.cover_letter:
I am excited to apply for the Bilingual Virtual Program Coordinator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Psychology graduate, I have been looking for an opportunity to work in a mental health setting where I can contribute to something meaningful while continuing to develop professionally. I enjoy remote work and the organization and communication that come with it, but what matters most to me is knowing that my work is helping people.

My interest in this field has grown even stronger since beginning my volunteer experience with the Alachua Crisis Center. It has reminded me how important it is to have people who are willing to listen, offer support, and help others through difficult moments. It has also made me realize how much I want my everyday work to be connected to making a difference in someone's life.

I previously worked at Nicaragua Recovery, a residential recovery program, where I supported patients through daily check-ins, activities, and recovery programming. I facilitated daily One Day at a Time reflection groups and translated the discussions into English for patients who did not speak Spanish so they could participate fully. I also interpreted conversations between patients and their outside caregivers, helping make communication easier and ensuring patients could better understand and express themselves. Later, I worked remotely as an Outreach Coordinator for the same program, contacting prospective patients, explaining the program, answering questions, and communicating with clinics and therapists about potential referrals.

In my current remote administrative position, I manage correspondence, organize information, communicate with customers, and coordinate with different departments. These responsibilities have strengthened my ability to stay organized, communicate clearly, and manage tasks independently. I would be excited to bring these skills into a mental health setting where the administrative work directly supports patients, families, and clinical teams.

As a native English and Spanish speaker with a degree in Psychology, I would value the opportunity to contribute to AWA's work with adolescents and their families. I am dependable, eager to learn, and genuinely motivated to build a career in a field where I can help others.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to speak with you about how my background and motivation could contribute to your team.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, creativity and passion for holistic wellness to AWA, contribute to your mission and be part of a team dedicated to making a positive impact.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to connect and discuss how my experience and values align with your organization.

Warm regards,
Christina Samuda

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. I hold a degree in Psychology and Human Development and Family Sciences and have hands-on experience working with adolescents and adults in behavioral health and residential treatment settings. In both psychiatric rehabilitation and substance use treatment facilities, I facilitated visual arts, stretching and movement, and psychosocial rehabilitation groups. Combined with my professional background in dance and creative expression, I bring a skill set that closely aligns with this position.

**Group Facilitation & Behavioral Health Experience**

My experience in residential behavioral health has involved facilitating groups designed to promote emotional well-being, social development, and personal growth. My psychosocial rehabilitation groups focused on strengthening everyday life skills, improving social functioning, developing healthy coping strategies, and increasing independence. Through structured activities, group discussions, and interactive exercises, I encouraged participants to practice communication, problem-solving, self-awareness, and positive interpersonal skills.

I also bring experience working with adolescents in youth development and residential settings. These experiences have strengthened my ability to build rapport, adapt activities to different developmental needs, manage group dynamics, and create supportive environments where young people feel comfortable participating.

**Dance & Creative Expression**

In addition to my behavioral health experience, I have a longstanding background in dance and movement. I studied classical dance at Miami Arts, served as a choreographer with Florida State University's Belly Dance Troupe, and have professional dance and performance experience.

I enjoy using movement and creative expression to encourage confidence, body awareness, self-expression, and personal growth. I would love to incorporate these interests into engaging group activities that help adolescents explore new ways to connect with themselves and others.

I am particularly drawn to AWA's approach to combining mental health support with creative and experiential programming. The opportunity to bring together my experience in group facilitation, behavioral health, adolescent development, and the arts is especially meaningful to me.

Thank you for your consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and experience could contribute to your programming and the adolescents you serve.

Sincerely,  
Athena V. Sullivan

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Team,

I'm excited to apply for the Creative Group Facilitator position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a background in Studio Art and Psychology, as well as experience in Special Education and Applied Behavior Analysis, I have always been drawn to the ways creativity can help us connect, express ourselves, and discover more about who we are. I would love the opportunity to bring this perspective into a setting that supports adolescents through their mental health journeys.

In my current role as a SpEd Art Teacher, I work with students with diverse learning needs, developing creative activities to encourage their exploration and independence. My approach to art is centered on the process rather than the final product; I believe the arts should be an opportunity to experiment, take risks, make mistakes, and express yourself without the pressure of getting something "right." My previous experience as an ABA Teacher has also taught me the importance of meeting individuals where they are and creating supportive environments where everyone feels welcome to participate.

My creative background extends beyond visual art to include writing, music, and theatre. These experiences have deepened my appreciation for the many ways people communicate and express themselves, and I'm drawn to opportunities that allow others to explore those possibilities.

My connection to art is also personal. Throughout my own experiences, creativity has been a meaningful way to process and make sense of my emotions. I've come to appreciate the value of having the space to process without judgement or expectations. This is an environment I hope to foster for others; one where individuals feel safe to explore their emotions, connect with each other, and perhaps even learn something new about themselves along the way.

I would be grateful for the chance to contribute my creativity and enthusiasm for the therapeutic arts to the AWA community. Thank you for your time and consideration.

Best,
Charity Ortiz, BA, RBT
